claim:
  status: "bounded read-only follow-up finding"
  statement: >-
    The retained Avvio subset provides five concrete design lessons for Get
    Modular, principally as contrasts between a semantic compiler and a
    host/lifecycle container. It does not justify adopting Avvio, importing its
    code, changing Core authority, or assigning lifecycle behavior to Core.
    This result can close the new O5 follow-up inspection, while the historical
    O5 record remains source-unavailable and must not be relabeled.
  evidenceClass: "source inspection only; no executed evidence"
  consensusQualification: >-
    Agreement with existing models or reviewers is not expert consensus.
    ADR-0008 itself says shared-model agreement remains review evidence
    (gm/docs/decisions/0008-bounded-internal-engine-self-composition.md:435-436),
    and the readiness report rejects worker count as consensus
    (gm/research/implementation-readiness/report.md:43-56).

authority:
  precedence:
    - >-
      Accepted ADR-0001 through ADR-0008 and ADR-0015, ARCH-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY,
      GM-REQ-V1, and digest-pinned artifacts.
    - >-
      Active architecture guidance, including current-contract.md, may explain
      implementation but cannot override accepted authority.
    - >-
      The readiness report and this Avvio inspection are non-authoritative
      research evidence.
    - >-
      oss/source-manifest.json explicitly labels the pack read-only
      supplemental input, not executable evidence, adoption, or accepted Get
      Modular authority (line 4).
  controllingBoundary: >-
    Get Modular compiles inert declarations and a complete profile into an
    immutable plan (gm/docs/architecture/system-boundary.md:13-15). It may not
    become a service locator or lifecycle authority (lines 69-70), and has no
    filesystem scan, dynamic import, network, clock, randomness, environment
    lookup, durable state, or hidden registry (lines 92-93).
  implementationStatus: >-
    There is no production package
    (gm/docs/architecture/current-contract.md:33-35). The readiness disposition
    remains NO-GO for the first tracked private Core source because the governed
    owner-start condition is absent
    (gm/research/implementation-readiness/report.md:5-12). ADR-0015 acceptance
    did not itself start implementation
    (gm/docs/decisions/0015-block-publication-surfaces-and-runtime-claims-while-decisions-stay-open.md:108-112).

observedBehavior:
  inspection:
    retainedFilesRead: 5
    executedEvidence: false
    description: >-
      All five listed Avvio files were read. No source was imported, installed,
      evaluated, or tested.
  lessons:
    - area: "identity"
      observation: >-
        Plugin names are derived from executable functions/options and may be
        replaced when a thenable resolves
        (lib/plugin.js:Plugin and Plugin.prototype.setFunc; lines 39 and 69).
      transferableLesson: >-
        Keep diagnostic labels useful, but keep semantic identity explicit,
        serializable, stable, and separate from executable names.
      nonTransferableRisk: >-
        Function names, metadata, or mutable resolved names cannot replace
        Get Modular's ModuleId, ImplementationId, CapabilityId, and local SlotId.
    - area: "declarations/dependencies"
      observation: >-
        Avvio registers executable functions plus options. Dependencies emerge
        from nested registration in the current context
        (README.md:118-130; index.js:Boot.prototype._addPlugin), while dynamic
        options may read the parent instance (README.md:671-699).
      transferableLesson: >-
        Dependency relationships must have one clear owner and missing/late
        registrations should fail visibly.
      nonTransferableRisk: >-
        Avvio's implicit tree is not an inert declaration language or complete
        profile. Get Modular requires every slot and provider binding explicitly,
        with ordered many dependencies; registration order is forbidden business
        semantics (ADR-0004:59-78).
    - area: "activation/order/scopes"
      observation: >-
        Root, plugin, ready, and close queues use serial fastq workers; nested
        plugins drain before their parent finishes
        (index.js:74,82,96,177-210; lib/plugin.js:Plugin.prototype.finish).
        override can create per-plugin inherited instances
        (README.md:943-995; index.js:Boot.prototype.override).
      transferableLesson: >-
        Make ordering and scope boundaries observable and reject registration
        after boot or after a parent loads (index.js:184-205).
      nonTransferableRisk: >-
        This is host activation and mutable context behavior. Get Modular's
        dependency-before-consumer order is graph data, not an instruction to
        execute, activate, or construct (ADR-0004:108-112).
    - area: "lifecycle/unload"
      observation: >-
        ready/start and onClose/close form an operational lifecycle; onClose
        handlers are queued with unshift and close waits for readiness
        (index.js:Boot.prototype.onClose, close, ready; README.md:373-407).
      transferableLesson: >-
        A Product Host should define explicit readiness, cleanup ordering, and
        terminal failure behavior around a compiled plan.
      nonTransferableRisk: >-
        Avvio close is not proof of unload, rollback, drain, fencing, recovery,
        generation cutover, or hot replacement. Those remain Product Host
        responsibilities; Core has no clock or lifecycle.
    - area: "compatibility/isolation/upgrades/errors"
      observation: >-
        The retained package is Avvio 9.3.0, CommonJS, with semver-ranged
        @fastify/error and fastq dependencies. Documentation advertises eight
        stable error codes, timeout-based failure, and stopping load until an
        error is handled (README.md:322-369,1200-1217). override provides object
        inheritance, not security isolation.
      transferableLesson: >-
        Stable, bounded, structured failure coordinates are valuable; invalid
        transitions should fail closed.
      nonTransferableRisk: >-
        The subset shows no capability-compatibility algebra, authorization,
        process/realm isolation, permission model, rolling upgrade, or recovery
        protocol. Runtime Error objects, function references, messages, timers,
        and mutable state cannot become Core diagnostics.

applicability:
  core: >-
    Apply only the lessons favoring explicit identity, explicit dependency
    ownership, deterministic validation, closed transitions, and structured
    failures. Core must remain inert and side-effect-free.
  productHost: >-
    Avvio is relevant only as a comparative example for a possible
    product-owned boot/cleanup adapter. Such an adapter would consume an
    authorized immutable plan and remain outside Core.
  extensionFoundation: >-
    No applicability was established for artifact trust, permissions,
    quarantine, isolation, upgrades, or plugin state.
  adoption: "not applicable and not recommended from this evidence"

benefits:
  - "Reinforces the value of explicit failure for late registration and incomplete work."
  - "Shows why construction order, readiness, and cleanup should be modeled together by one host authority."
  - "Provides a concrete counterexample supporting Get Modular's ban on registration order as semantic input."
  - "Supports keeping diagnostic identity separate from executable implementation identity."

failureModes:
  - "Implicit nested registration can hide dependencies and make authoring order operationally significant."
  - "Mutable inherited contexts can leak state or collide with host properties; they are not isolation."
  - "Timer and Date-based timeouts introduce runtime scheduling and clock dependence."
  - "Callback and Promise completion styles enlarge the lifecycle state space despite duplicate-completion guards."
  - "Failure handling can skip later non-after plugins; this is partial boot behavior, not atomic compilation."
  - "Cleanup callbacks do not demonstrate resource rollback after partially completed activation."
  - "Semver-ranged implementation dependencies do not define capability-contract compatibility."

counterexamples:
  - >-
    Calling Avvio graph-based does not make it a semantic graph compiler: its
    graph is formed while executable plugins register children.
  - >-
    Serial queue order can be correct for boot yet invalid for Get Modular,
    where registration order must not affect plans or diagnostics.
  - >-
    A stable AVV error code is not equivalent to Get Modular's closed,
    deterministically ordered, capped diagnostic algebra.
  - >-
    An inherited child object is scoped context sharing, not sandboxing or
    process isolation.
  - >-
    onClose supports shutdown callbacks but does not prove unload, hot upgrade,
    generation fencing, routing drain, or durable recovery.

recommendedDecision:
  disposition: "do not adopt; do not accept or alter any architecture decision"
  recommendation: >-
    Record this as a new read-only O5 follow-up result that closes the prepared
    source-inspection lane only. Preserve the historical source-unavailable
    status. Retain the five lessons as bounded comparative guidance: explicit
    identities, explicit dependencies, deterministic graph output, and bounded
    diagnostics belong in Core; activation, scoped instances, readiness,
    timeouts, error recovery, close/unload, and upgrades belong in a
    product-owned host. Do not implement Core or import Avvio based on this
    result.

    Consider Avvio only for a specifically authorized product-host adapter, never
    Core, after that host supplies lifecycle requirements and ownership.
  - "Inspect the complete pinned source, dependency lock, types, tests, changelog, and security/release history."

  - "Prove adapter isolation from Core declarations, plans, diagnostics, public types, and packed dependencies."
  - >-
    Require a new accepted decision before any package dependency, public
    surface, lifecycle authority, or architecture-boundary change.
